author: reek
body: H12: the Historian role walks the supersession chain for any annotation and renders attribution + verdicts. Given a starting annotation hash, follows supersession-target until the latest entry; at each step records the author and any verdicts attached.

author: reek
body: The chain is a finite list -- we terminate either when no successor is mapped or when we revisit a hash (loop guard).

author: reek
body: walk-history follows the supersession map from the starting hash, looking up each annotation's body and verdicts. Maximum chain length is bounded -- 64 hops should be far more than any realistic supersession chain.

author: reek
body: The loop guard is the set of hashes already walked. Without it a supersession cycle is bounded only by max-chain-depth, so A superseded by B superseded by A does not terminate at the cycle -- it runs all 64 hops and reports 64 steps over two annotations, each listed thirty-two times. The prose above has always promised this guard; it is kept in a Hamt keyed by hash, which is how the repo itself keys annotations, so it admits exactly the hashes the walk can encounter.

author: reek
body: The supersession key is an annotation hash, but verdicts are keyed by proposal id. The two are equal only when a proposal was authored from the same content as the underlying annotation -- which is the H7 publish-proposal flow's invariant. Look up by hash; empty list if no proposal carried this hash.
